extracted.intended_audience: users of Singular/Plural performing non-commutative algebra computations (mathematicians / computer-algebra practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation and reference for the Plural (non-commutative) subsystem of Singular: definitions, procedures, and usage guidance for G-algebras, Groebner bases, syzygies, Letterplace methods, and library routines. Covers syntax, purposes, notes, examples and implementation restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ringlist (decompose ring)
rubrics_metrics.description: decomposes a ring/qring into a list of 6 (or 4 in the commutative case) components. The first 4 components are common for commutative and non-commutative cases; the 5th and 6th appear only in the non-commutative case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Components include (among others): (5) upper triangular square matrix with nonzero upper triangle containing structural coefficients of a G-algebra (matrix C), and (6) square matrix containing structural polynomials of a G-algebra (matrix D). After modifying a list acquired with ringlist, construct a corresponding ring with ring(list). Example shown for quantized Weyl algebra: obtain list l = ringlist(RS), modify l[5] and l[6] and regenerate ring with ring(l). See also ring and related sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: slimgb (compute slim left Groebner basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: returns a left Groebner basis of a left ideal or module with respect to the global monomial ordering of the basering. Designed to keep polynomials or vectors slim (short with small coefficients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation details: described in diploma thesis by Michael Brickenstein. Best results over function fields (parameters). May not be optimal for weighted degree orderings. Supported options: prot (protocol output) and redSB (return reduced Groebner basis). Protocol messages: M[n,m] = parallel reduction of n elements with m non-zero outputs; b = an exchange trick; e = adds a reductor with non-minimal leading term. Works for graded commutative algebras but not general GR-algebras (use qslimgb instead). Examples: computing slimgb for U(sl_2) and for exterior algebras are shown; comparison with std demonstrates equality in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: std (compute left Groebner basis / standard basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: returns a left Groebner basis of an ideal or module with respect to the monomial ordering of the basering. Optional second argument (poly or vector) can be used to extend an already computed basis by one generator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To view progress of long computations use option(prot). Examples show use on U(sl_2) and quantum algebras; console output may include product and chain criterion statistics. Use option(redSB) and option(redTail) when reduced bases are needed. See also references to Groebner bases in G-algebras.

rubrics_metrics.name: subst (substitute variable by polynomial)
rubrics_metrics.description: substitutes a ring variable by a polynomial. Works for poly, vector, ideal or module as the first argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: in U(sl_2) algebra, subst(e,h^3) applied to poly C = e*f*h yields explicit expanded polynomial; subst(f,e+f) example shown. Use to perform symbol replacements in non-commutative context.

rubrics_metrics.name: syz (compute syzygy module)
rubrics_metrics.description: computes the first syzygy (module of relations) of the given generators of an ideal or module; returns a module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Plural syz returns left syzygies only. If S is a matrix of a left syzygy module for M, then transpose(S)*transpose(M) = 0 (but in general M*S != 0). Syzygy modules depend on a choice of generators but are unique up to direct summands. Examples show computing syzygies, verifying transpose relations, and that commutative syzygy properties need not hold in non-commutative setting. Options redSB and redTail recommended for completely reduced bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: twostd (two-sided Groebner basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: returns a left Groebner basis of the two-sided ideal generated by the input, treating the input set as two-sided generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark: some algebras have no nontrivial two-sided ideals (e.g., Weyl algebras). Examples: compute twostd(i) for generators i in U(sl_2), print compact presentations of J and compare with one-sided std(I). One can compute NF(J,I) to find elements present in the two-sided ideal but not in the one-sided ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: vdim (vector space dimension of factor-module)
rubrics_metrics.description: computes the vector space dimension of the factor-module that equals ring (or free module) modulo the ideal (resp. submodule) generated by the leading terms of the given generators. Returns -1 if infinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the generators form a Groebner basis, vdim equals the vector space dimension of the factor-module. Note: in the non-commutative case, a ring modulo an ideal has a ring structure iff the ideal is two-sided. Example: computing vdim after std on an ideal in U(sl_2) yields 21. See also kbase and std sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: G-algebra (definition / eligibility conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: An algebra A = K<x1,...,xn | {xj xi = cij · xi xj + dij, 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n}> is a G-algebra if: (1) there is a monomial well-ordering < on K[x1,...,xn] such that for all i<j, LM(dij) < xixj, and (2) non-degeneracy conditions NDCijk = 0 for all 1 ≤ i < j < k ≤ n, where NDCijk is an explicit combination ensuring associativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-degeneracy conditions ensure associativity. LM(dij) < xixj guarantees that the PBW monomials remain a basis. Plural provides nc_algebra(C,D) to initialize a G-algebra from matrices C (coefficients) and D (polynomials). Plural does not automatically check NDCs; library provides ndcond to check them. See mathematical background and references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties of G-algebras (expected consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a G-algebra then: A has a PBW basis; A is left and right noetherian; A is an integral domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These properties follow from the defining conditions; they justify algorithmic approaches (finite basis behavior, termination aspects) used in Plural. Reference to formal theorem in the manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting up a G-algebra (procedural requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: To set up a G-algebra one must: (1) define a commutative ring R = K[x1,...,xn] with a monomial ordering (gives field K, variables, ordering); (2) define strictly n×n upper triangular matrices C (numbers cij for i<j) and D (polynomials dij for i<j); (3) call initialization function nc_algebra(C,D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ordering must be a monomial well-ordering. Plural's nc_algebra accepts C and D; Plural does not automatically check non-degeneracy conditions (use ndcond from nctools.lib). Examples illustrate constructing C and D via ringlist and then creating a new ring with ring(l).

rubrics_metrics.name: Left Groebner basis in G-algebras (definition / minimality)
rubrics_metrics.description: A finite set G ⊂ I (left A-submodule of Ar) is a left Groebner basis iff L(G) = L(I), i.e., for any f ∈ I\0 there exists g∈G with LM(g) dividing LM(f). G is minimal (reduced) if 0 ∉ G and LM(g) ∉ L(G\{g}) for all g∈G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimality can be achieved by deleting g for which some h∈G\{g} has LM(h) | LM(g). In non-commutative/plural algorithms, only well-orderings are generally used. For a set G, f is completely reduced wrt G if no monomial of f is in L(G). See Section on left normal forms and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Left Normal Form (NF) properties
rubrics_metrics.description: A map NF: Ar × {G | G a left Groebner basis} → Ar is a left normal form if for any f∈Ar and left Groebner basis G: (i) NF(0|G)=0; (ii) if NF(f|G) ≠ 0 then LM(g) does not divide LM(NF(f|G)) for all g∈G; (iii) f − NF(f|G) ∈ A·G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NF(f|G) is a left normal form of f with respect to G, but such a map is not unique. Plural works with left normal forms only; use NF to test membership and to obtain reduced representatives modulo left ideal/module.

rubrics_metrics.name: Left ideal membership test
rubrics_metrics.description: For a left Groebner basis G of I, an element f belongs to I if and only if the left normal form NF(f|G) = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NF with a computed left Groebner basis to decide membership. Examples and procedures in the manual demonstrate NF usage for ideals and modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syzygies (definition and Plural behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: A left syzygy between elements f1,...,fk ⊂ Ar is a k-tuple (g1,...,gk)∈Ak with sum_{i} g_i f_i = 0. The set of all left syzygies is a left submodule S of Ak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plural works with left syzygies only. If S is matrix of left syzygy module for generators M, transpose(S)*transpose(M)=0. Syzygy modules depend on generators but are unique up to direct summands. Examples: computing syz(K) and verifying tst = ideal(transpose(S)*transpose(K)) has size 0; also demonstrating that commutative syzygy properties may fail in non-commutative case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free resolutions (construction and exactness checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: A free resolution of M = Ar/I is a long exact sequence ... → F2 --B2→ F1 --B1→ F0 → M → 0 with transpose(B_{i+1})·transpose(B_i)=0 and columns of B1 generating I. Resolutions over factor-algebras need not be of finite length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plural provides procedures (e.g., mres) to compute resolutions and outputs matrices l[1], l[2], ...; exactness can be checked by computing transpose products and checking ideal sizes (size(ideal(TST))==0). Example shows resolution of ideal in U(sl_2) and verification of exactness via matrix multiplications producing zero ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalized Hilbert Syzygy Theorem (resolution length bound)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a G-algebra A generated by n variables, there exists a free resolution of length ≤ n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides an upper bound for resolution length used when attempting to compute finite free resolutions in Plural. Example references and usage are provided in the manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graded commutative algebras (SCA) — definition and features
rubrics_metrics.description: Polynomial graded commutative algebras are factors of tensor products of commutative algebras with an exterior algebra over a field K, with a natural Z2-grading: anti-commutative generators degree 1, commutative generators degree 0. They can be viewed as super-commutative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinctive features: zero divisors occur iff number of anti-commutative generators m>0 (because yi*yi=0). Unlike other non-commutative algebras, any monomial ordering is allowed provided only non-commutative variables are global; commutative variables may be local. Implementation: use superCommutative procedure from nctools.lib; examples show ring declaration variants, use of std for Groebner bases (global ordering required), and results of std with specific ideals. Reference: Ph.D. thesis by Oleksandr Motsak (2010).

rubrics_metrics.name: Letterplace — free associative algebra and two-sided Groebner bases
rubrics_metrics.description: Free associative algebra K< x1,...,xn > has monomials = words over xi; a monomial ordering on the free monoid X must be a well-ordering satisfying compatibility with concatenation. For a subset G⊂T, L(G) is the two-sided leading ideal T·{lm(g)}·T. G is a two-sided Groebner basis if L(G)=L(I) (i.e., for every f∈I there is g∈G whose lm divides lm(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions of division (v divides w if w = p v s) and properties of monomial orderings are given. Because free algebra is not Noetherian, two-sided Groebner bases of finitely generated ideals may be infinite; computations are commonly done up to degree bounds and using Letterplace techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letterplace correspondence (encoding and shifting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Encode monomials (words) xi1 xi2 ... xim as letterplace monomials x(i1|1) x(i2|2) ... x(im|m) in the commutative letterplace algebra K[X×N]. There is a 1-to-1 correspondence between graded two-sided ideals of free algebra and letterplace ideals; computations occur in the (truncated) letterplace algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letterplace monomials are multilinear in places; letterplace ideals are closed under algebra operations and simultaneous shifting of places by any natural number. Use the truncated letterplace algebra with a chosen degree bound to obtain finite computations. See LL09 and LL13 references for theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letterplace usage workflow and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended workflow: define a commutative ring K[X] with a degree well-ordering; pick degree bound d and run makeLetterplaceRing(d) to create letterplace ring; define ideal I in letterplace encoding and run letplaceGBasis (or system("freegb",I,d,n)); conversions between letterplace and string forms via lp2lstr and lst2str.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided show creation of letterplace ring, computing letplaceGBasis, and converting results back to original ring notation. Alternatively use freeGBasis (from freegb.lib) for different encodings without conversion tools. Options option(redSB) and option(redTail) should be used; option(redSB); option(redTail); must be activated per release notes. Use option(prot) and option(mem) to monitor progress and memory usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letterplace restrictions and implementation notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Current restrictions: stable implementation for homogeneous input only; computations with quasi-homogeneous and general inhomogeneous ideals are under development (no automatic checks). Because the free algebra is not Noetherian, an explicit degree bound must be provided and stored in the ring object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: makeLetterplaceRing stores the degree bound inside the ring structure so letplaceGBasis in such a ring does not require the bound argument. Required options: option(redSB) and option(redTail) must be activated. Recommended to run with option(prot); option(mem); for activity journal and memory usage. Further functionality available in freegb.lib and fpadim.lib for conversions, arithmetic, normal forms, finiteness checks and dimension computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monomial orderings for non-commutative algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: In general non-commutative algorithms operate with well-orderings only (unless dealing with graded commutative algebras). The chosen monomial ordering must be global for Plural computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Sections on PLURAL, Monomial orderings and Term orderings for allowed orderings. Note: For any computation in Plural the monomial ordering must be a global ordering. For graded-commutative SCA, commutative variables can be local while non-commutative variables must be global.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-degeneracy conditions (NDC) checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-degeneracy conditions NDCijk = 0 (explicit formula given) must hold for a GR-algebra to ensure associativity; Plural does not automatically check them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use procedure ndcond from the nctools library (Section 7.7.16.3) to check NDCs. The manual notes that these conditions simply ensure associativity; examples and references provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal/reduced Groebner basis construction guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: A Groebner basis G is minimal (reduced) if 0 ∉ G and for all g ∈ G, LM(g) ∉ L(G \ {g}). Any Groebner basis can be made minimal by successively deleting g with LM(h) | LM(g) for some h ∈ G \ {g}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use option(redSB) for obtaining reduced bases when available. Examples show that slimgb and std with redSB produce comparable Groebner bases and NF comparisons can confirm equality of bases.
